backlog.spec: Change WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.3 so more of the 300s budget is spent at peak LR. Keep FINAL_LR_FRAC at 0.0.
backlog.title: Lower warmdown ratio to 0.3

backlog.spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.7 to test a longer linear decay, which often helps in short fixed-time runs.
backlog.title: Higher warmdown ratio 0.7

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO = 0.03 to avoid early instability from the high embedding and scalar LRs.
backlog.title: Small LR warmup

backlog.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.05 so the LR does not decay fully to zero.
backlog.title: Final LR fraction 0.05

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18. This gives more optimizer steps in the 300s budget. Keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE at 64, so gradient accumulation halves.
backlog.title: Halve total batch size

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**17 for many more steps. Scale MATRIX_LR down by about 0.8 if training looks unstable.
backlog.title: Quarter total batch size

backlog.spec: Set DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE = 32 and keep TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE the same. This tests whether less memory pressure improves throughput. Revert if tokens/sec drops.
backlog.title: Device batch 32

backlog.spec: Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.05.
backlog.title: Matrix LR 0.05

backlog.spec: Lower EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.4.
backlog.title: Embedding LR 0.4

backlog.spec: Double UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.008.
backlog.title: Unembedding LR 0.008

backlog.spec: Halve SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.25 to stabilize the per-layer scalars.
backlog.title: Scalar LR 0.25

backlog.spec: Lower Muon WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.1. The run is short, so less regularization may help.
backlog.title: Weight decay 0.1

backlog.spec: Raise WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.3.
backlog.title: Weight decay 0.3

backlog.spec: Set ADAM_BETAS = (0.8, 0.99) for smoother second-moment estimates.
backlog.title: Adam beta2 0.99

backlog.spec: Set ADAM_BETAS = (0.9, 0.95).
backlog.title: Adam beta1 0.9

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 6 and ASPECT_RATIO = 85 (dim rounded to a multiple of HEAD_DIM, 512 here). This tests a smaller, faster model that sees more tokens in 300s.
backlog.title: Depth 6 wider ratio

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 10 with ASPECT_RATIO = 51 so dim stays near 512. Check that it is a multiple of HEAD_DIM. This tests a deeper model with fewer steps.
backlog.title: Depth 10

backlog.spec: Set HEAD_DIM = 64 for more attention heads at the same width.
backlog.title: Head dim 64

backlog.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN to "SSSSL" or "SL". Try "SSL" if the model builds the pattern by cycling. This tests how much full attention is needed. The last layer must stay L.
backlog.title: Window pattern SSSSL-like

backlog.spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN = "SSSS" so the only full-context layer is the final one, which is forced to L. This cuts attention cost.
backlog.title: All-short windows except last

backlog.spec: If the forward pass has a logit softcap (e.g. 15), lower it to 10. If there is none, add 15*tanh(logits/15) before the loss.
backlog.title: Untied-style logit softcap tweak

backlog.spec: If the MLP uses relu(x)**2, keep it. Otherwise switch to relu squared. Also set the MLP hidden size to 3.5x instead of 4x to save compute.
backlog.title: ReLU squared to SwiGLU-free tweak: GELU check

backlog.spec: Zero-initialize the attention c_proj and MLP c_proj weights if not already done. This makes residual blocks start as identity.
backlog.title: Zero-init output projections

backlog.spec: Initialize the token embedding with std 0.5 instead of 1.0, or the reverse if it is already below 1. This tests embedding scale sensitivity.
backlog.title: Smaller init std for embeddings

backlog.spec: Add torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0) before optimizer.step(). This guards against loss spikes at high LR.
backlog.title: Gradient clipping 1.0

backlog.spec: Shorten the Muon momentum ramp from 0 to 0.95 to complete in about 100 steps. Alternatively raise the final momentum to 0.97.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warmup shorter

backlog.spec: Reduce Muon's Newton-Schulz iterations from 5 to 4 to save time per step, if the code allows it.
backlog.title: Muon Newton-Schulz steps 4

backlog.spec: Replace the linear warmdown with a cosine shape: lr = 0.5*(1+cos(pi*p)) over the warmdown phase, keeping the same WARMDOWN_RATIO.
backlog.title: Time-based LR schedule with cosine decay

backlog.spec: Make sure the eval and train batches have fixed shapes and mark the compile call as fullgraph=True, dynamic=False. This lowers recompiles and gains steps in the fixed time budget. Keep the evaluation call untouched.
backlog.title: Disable torch.compile dynamic overhead via fixed shapes

backlog.spec: In the model's init_weights (or wherever block weights are initialized), set the attention output projection (c_proj) and the MLP output projection weights to zeros so every residual block starts as identity. Leave all other init unchanged. Keep everything else the same and run the standard 300 s.
backlog.title: Zero-init attention and MLP output projections

backlog.spec: Before the optimizer step in the training loop, after the accumulated backward passes, call torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0). Make no other change. It tests whether the small-batch regime (2**17) benefits from stabilised updates.
backlog.title: Gradient clipping at 1.0

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**16 so each optimizer step is a single microbatch with no grad accumulation (64 x 2048 = 131k tokens, so check the actual sequence length; if 2**16 is not divisible by DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE*MAX_SEQ_LEN, use DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 32). Keep the LRs unchanged. This gives roughly 2x more optimizer steps in 300 s.
backlog.title: Batch 2**16 with device batch 64

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.03 so the LR rises linearly from 0 over the first 3% of the time budget. Muon and Adam at high LR with small batches may be unstable at step 0. Change nothing else.
backlog.title: Cosine-free linear warmup of 3 percent

backlog.spec: For the first 25% of the time budget, truncate each batch to the first half of the sequence length (reshape or slice inputs and targets to T/2 and keep the token count per step constant by using 2x the rows if easy; otherwise just use shorter sequences). Then switch to full length. This gives cheaper early steps. If torch.compile recompiles, mark the shapes as dynamic=False and accept one extra compile, which is not counted in the budget.
backlog.title: Sequence-length curriculum

backlog.spec: If the model uses value embeddings on alternating layers, restrict them to only the last 2 layers, saving parameters and memory bandwidth. This lets the model trade capacity for more steps. If there are no value embeddings, skip this and instead scale the residual stream lambda init to 0.5 for x0 mixing. Make a single minimal edit.
backlog.title: Untied value-embedding removal / lighter value embeds

backlog.spec: Change the Muon momentum schedule so that momentum ramps from 0.85 to 0.95 over the first 100 steps instead of the current slower ramp (or if there is no ramp, set it constant at 0.9). The small-batch run has many steps, so a shorter ramp should reach good momentum earlier.
backlog.title: Muon momentum 0.9 with shorter warmup

backlog.spec: Keep DEPTH=6 and set ASPECT_RATIO=107, so model_dim is about 640 (must be a multiple of HEAD_DIM 128; 640 gives 5 heads). Check that it fits memory at DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64. This tests whether more width at the same depth helps now that steps are cheap. Avoid changing anything else.
backlog.title: Bigger depth-6 width via ASPECT_RATIO 107

backlog.spec: Make Muon's weight decay follow the schedule WEIGHT_DECAY * (1 - progress), where progress is time elapsed over the time budget, instead of a constant 0.2. Update it each step in the optimizer param group alongside the LR. This reduces regularisation late, when the LR is also annealing.
backlog.title: Weight-decay linear decay to zero

backlog.spec: Maintain an exponential moving average of the model parameters (decay 0.999, updated every step with torch._foreach_lerp_ on a copied parameter list). Before the final evaluation call, swap the EMA weights into the model, without touching the evaluation code itself. Warmdown already reduces noise, so use this only if it adds under 15 lines. Otherwise skip.
backlog.title: EMA of weights for evaluation

backlog.spec: Maintain an exponential moving average copy of the model parameters (decay 0.999, updated every optimizer step with torch._foreach_lerp_ on a bf16/fp32 shadow copy). Before the final evaluation call, swap the EMA weights into the model (copy_ into parameters). Do not touch the evaluation call itself; only copy the weights in just before it. Keep the code short.
backlog.title: EMA of weights for evaluation

backlog.spec: After the gradient accumulation loop and before optimizer.step(), call torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0). Small batches (2**17) are noisy, so clipping may stabilise early training with the high Adam LRs.
backlog.title: Gradient clipping at 1.0

backlog.spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY to 0.3 and scale the Muon weight decay each step by (1 - progress), where progress is the time-budget fraction already used. This gives strong regularization early and none at the end of the warmdown.
backlog.title: Weight decay 0.3 with linear decay to zero

backlog.spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO=0.7 and FINAL_LR_FRAC=0.05 together. With few steps in 300 s, a longer anneal with a nonzero floor may improve final loss. Change only these two constants.
backlog.title: Longer warmdown 0.7 with final LR 0.05

backlog.spec: Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.06 (Muon). The smaller 2**17 batch changed the optimum, and the LR has not been retuned since. Change only this constant.
backlog.title: Matrix LR 0.06 with smaller batch-noise tolerance

backlog.spec: Set ADAM_BETAS to (0.9, 0.99) for the embedding, unembedding and scalar Adam groups. Smoother second-moment estimates may help with the noisy small batches.
backlog.title: Adam beta2 0.99 and beta1 0.9

backlog.spec: Find the logit softcap constant in the model forward (likely 30 or 15, applied as cap*tanh(x/cap)). Change it to 15, or to 30 if it is already 15. This is a one-number change that alters output logit saturation.
backlog.title: Logit softcap lowered to 15

backlog.spec: Disable the value-embedding residual path in attention (the per-layer value embeddings added to v, and their gate). Remove the parameters and their optimizer group. This frees parameters and time per step, so more steps fit in 300 s. It is a bold simplification. If the removal is too invasive, skip the gate and zero out the embeddings only on alternate layers.
backlog.title: Remove value embeddings

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH=4 and ASPECT_RATIO=128 so model_dim is 512 and there are 4 heads of 128. A shallower model gets more steps in 300 s. Keep HEAD_DIM=128 and make sure WINDOW_PATTERN still works for 4 layers (the last layer must be full attention).
backlog.title: Depth 4 wide model for more steps

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 3*2**15 (about 98K tokens) with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 48 so each step is 2 microbatches. This is an intermediate batch size between 2**16 (worse) and 2**17. Ensure that TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE is divisible by DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE times the sequence length. Otherwise use DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 32 with 3 accumulation steps.
backlog.title: Batch 2**17 using device batch 32 with 4 microbatches off, torch.compile on larger fused loss

incumbent.description: Reduce TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**17 (grad accumulation 2 steps at device batch 64) to get ~4x more optimizer steps in the 300s budget.
